ember-gradient.$description: Ember Gradient — Brand mark, Poly logo, the sole chromatic accent — warm orange fading to signal red, used only on identity, never on body UI

porcelain.$description: Porcelain — Page canvas, card surfaces, inverted text on dark photo backgrounds

onyx.$description: Onyx — Dark borders and separators for elevated surfaces and inverted UI. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

graphite.$description: Graphite — Secondary text, hairline borders, icon fills, the slight warmth that keeps near-black from feeling clinical

ash.$description: Ash — Shadow tone used in the soft-etched link treatment, muted dividers

haffer-variable.$description: Primary display serif for headlines at 30–53px. Weight 450 is anti-convention — most product sites push display to 600–700, but Haffer at 450 keeps headlines warm and editorial rather than commanding. Activating liga and ss04 unlocks the alternative g and stylised letterforms that give the wordmark its personality.

bogue.$description: Companion serif at regular weight, used for badge labels and secondary serif moments where Haffer 450 would feel too heavy. Tighter tracking at -0.03em distinguishes it from Haffer.

haffer.$description: Static fallback for small serif text — 15px badges, 24px sub-serial moments

inter.$description: All UI, body, nav, button labels, helper text. Inter at 400 handles body, 600 carries subheadings and button text. The -0.02em tracking matches the serif family, keeping the type system visually unified.
